::: proof

**Using @thm-deriv-matrix-vector:**

Since $\vx$ is constant with respect to $\vb$,
$A = \tp{\vx}$ is a constant $1 \times p$ matrix.
Applying @thm-deriv-matrix-vector with $\vecf{v} = \vb$
(so $\deriv{\vb}\vb = \matr{I}$):

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vb}(\tp{\vx}\vb)
&= \paren{\deriv{\vb}\vb} \tp{(\tp{\vx})} \\
&= \matr{I} \cdot \vx \\
&= \vx
\ea
$$

:::
